Metro Neighborhood Atlas

Every neighborhood (2010 census tract) in the Colorado Front Range (Fort Collins and Greeley down through Denver to Colorado Springs and Woodland Park), the Salt Lake area, the Seattle area and Whatcom County (Bellingham), scored with the atlas criteria plus the newer layers: school test growth, play-based and top-rated pre-K, hands-on K–8 schools and access to a walkable core. Pick a metro, choose what the map shows, set your weights, and click any neighborhood for its full profile.

    How to read it

    • Scores. Each criterion is a percentile among 15,188 western neighborhoods (100 is best), except Walkable core, which is access out of 100. The score is your weighted average; the rank compares neighborhoods in the same metro (only in-budget ones when Budget is ticked). Score colors stretch from the metro’s weakest to strongest neighborhoods by default, so the best of each metro looks equally green; switch “Score colors compare” to All four metros to put every metro on one scale. The other map measures are already on a shared scale (pre-K within each state).
    • Schools is test results of public schools within 3 km, grades 3–8, 2009–19 (Stanford Education Data Archive). Growth is how much those students improve each year versus the U.S. rate; it reflects the schools more than who lives nearby. Both compare across all four metros.
    • Pre-K has two numbers: play-based programs nearby (Montessori, Waldorf, Reggio-inspired, nature-based) and top-rated ones (NAEYC-accredited, Colorado Shines 4–5, Washington Early Achievers 4–5). They are percentiles within each state; Utah’s top-rated number counts NAEYC only. Untick approaches under “Play-based pre-K counts” to score only the ones you care about; the map, table, profile and score follow.
    • K–8 counts public and charter Montessori, Waldorf-method, EL Education and IB Primary Years schools within about a 20-minute drive, across Colorado, Utah and Washington.
    • Walkable core is access to a walkable town centre: full within about 5 km, fading out by 15 km, scaled by the centre’s size (set Small-core credit in Weights).
    • Dots mark specific places. Montessori: preschools from the state licensing lists and NAEYC, plus public and charter Montessori K–8 schools (a school and preschool on the same site share one dot). Reggio-inspired: programs that call themselves Reggio-inspired on their own site or listing (searched October 10, 2026), so expect gaps; none turned up in Whatcom County. Arts high schools: public and charter schools with an audition or arts focus for grades 9–12. Pins marked approximate in their details were placed by street address by hand; The Center School in Seattle may have closed. Click a dot for details.
    • Grey neighborhoods have no value for the measure shown, or fall outside the budget when Budget is ticked. Home values are Zillow’s neighborhood or ZIP figures.
